title: Cachinncak / Orawac Brook
summary: Orawac or Orowoc is a brook placename in Islip, connected with the modern Orowoc Creek and older Cachinncak boundary-marker name.
address_label: Orowoc Creek / Orawac Brook, Bay Shore-East Islip, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Orowoc Creek point from USGS/topographic coordinates; original Cachinncak boundary mark was at the head of the brook and needs location review.
why_this_matters: Cachinncak / Orawac Brook preserves layered names for an Islip waterway now associated with Orowoc Creek, including language interpreted as a marked place or boundary. That meaning shows how brooks could serve as more than physical features: they could mark limits, guide movement, and organize land relationships. South Shore waterways remain part of Indigenous geography and memory, even when later English names such as Paper Mill Brook entered written sources.
introduction_content: Orawac, also written Orowoc, is a brook name in Islip sometimes associated with Paper Mill Brook. The existing Cachinncak record is the safest place to keep this related Orawac/Orowoc creek-name cluster together.
history_content: The placename brings together the Orowoc Creek location, the older Cachinncak boundary-marker context, and related Islip creek names. Dated source details appear in the historic moments below, where each event can carry its own reference.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Cachinncak, Orawac, Orawack, Orowoc, Oriwic, and Paper Mill Brook. Cachinncak is interpreted as a beginning place or place of beginning. Orawac/Orowoc is interpreted as a wilderness or wild water-place, tied to the vacant-land description around the brook.

Why Place Names Matter

“The names in the landscape encapsulate its history, and through these names this history can be ‘read’ like a book printed on topography instead of paper.”

— Gunnell et al., Twelve Movements: Aspects of the Engagement with the Supernatural Landscape (2024), section discussing place-names and memory
whereintheworld_content: Approximate general point at modern Orowoc Creek in Islip. The map placement is for orientation, not an exact coordinate for the older boundary marker or patent landscape.
